Scope `accounts:read`. D7 class A.

item.name: List the accounts bound to this key

request.description:
The accounts this key may reach (spec D4), which may be a strict
subset of the workspace's accounts. Every other `/v1` read is scoped
to this set, and `?account_id=` on a collection names one of them.

Not paginated: the binding is bounded server-side, and a key bound to
more accounts than an unfiltered listing supports is REFUSED with
`invalid_request` rather than truncated — a silently truncated tenancy
set would show as accounts that exist in the Postora UI and not in the
API. `next_cursor` i

A conversation belonging to a bound account whose platform is not
`whatsapp` answers `unsupported_capability` (422), not
`resource_not_found`: the account IS in the binding and
`GET /v1/accounts` lists it, so denying its existence would be
misleading. There is no per-message table to read for it.

Scope `conversations:read`. D7 class A.

item.name: List the messages in one conversation

request.description:
Ordered by `timestamp` descending, then by id — newest first. The
conversation's binding is checked exactly as it is for
`GET /v1/conversations/{id}`; this sub-resource is never laxer than
its parent.

Scope `messages:read`. D7 class A.

item.name: List WhatsApp conversations across the bound accounts

request.description:
Ordered by `last_message_at` descending, then by id — the pair, not
the timestamp alone, because timestamps collide during history sync
and a cursor on the timestamp alone would either re-emit a whole
colliding group or drop all but one of it.

Conversations with no `last_message_at` are excluded: that column is
the cursor's sort key.

Default scope is ALL bound accounts, each row labelled with
`account_id` (spec D11) — never an implicit single-account default,
which would change meaning the day

Scoped to the presented key's workspace. A `media_id` belonging to
another workspace is indistinguishable from one that never existed —
both answer `resource_not_found`.

Returns metadata only. `GET /v1/media/{id}/download` is not part of
this version: it is the endpoint that would create a partner-facing
URL TTL contract, and it is not needed in order to send a message.

Scope `media:read`. D7 class A.

item.name: Upload a file for later use in a message

request.description:
Accepts either `multipart/form-data` with a `file` part, or JSON with
`data` (base64, or a `data:` URL) plus optional `filename` and

around the controls.

**The bytes are sniffed on every upload** and a declared type that
disagrees with them is REFUSED, not corrected: a mismatch means the
client's idea of the file and the file itself have diverged, and the

item.name: Create a post for explicit target accounts

request.description:
**Only posts created through this operation are addressable by the
`/v1/posts` routes.** A post created in the Postora UI answers
`resource_not_found` on every one of them, permanently and by design.

`targets` is required and must be a non-empty array of `acc_` ids;
there is no "publish to everything" shorthand. Every target must be
bound to the calling key and all targets must belong to one Postora
user. An unbound target answers `resource_not_found`, never 403, so
the caller learns nothing ab

Only posts created through `POST /v1/posts` are addressable. A Postora
UI-created post, a post outside the caller's workspace and an id that
is not well-formed all answer `resource_not_found`,
indistinguishably.

`id` is the opaque `post_` identifier. Provider post ids are never
accepted as the primary id.

Scope `posts:read`. D7 class A.

Returns one row per target result from `platform_posts`. One platform
succeeding while another fails is represented faithfully, never
collapsed into one verdict. Provider ids and URLs appear only as the
clearly named `provider_post_id` and `provider_post_url` fields; the
primary post and account ids remain opaque `post_` and `acc_` ids.

Only posts created through `POST /v1/posts` are addressable. A Postora
UI-created post answers `resource_not_found`, permanently and by
design.

Scope `posts:re

Clears `scheduled_at` and parks the post as `pending`, where the
scheduler cannot pick it up. A post that is already `pending` returns
the same post as an idempotent success; a post in any other state
answers `invalid_request` (400).

This operation emits no webhook event. There is no certified
`post.unscheduled` event type.

Scope `posts:schedule`. D7 class C.

Sets the post to `scheduled` with the supplied `scheduled_at`. The
timestamp is required and must be ISO-8601 with an explicit offset,
for example `2026-09-03T14:00:00Z`; a value without an offset answers
`invalid_request` (400). Only a `pending` or `scheduled` post can be
scheduled.

There is no `POST /v1/posts/{id}/publish` yet. Scheduling is how a
partner publishes: the scheduler picks the post up and publishes it.

Scope `posts:schedule`. D7 class C.

The response carries `secret` — the **only** time it is returned
other than a rotation. Store it: Postora cannot show it again.

`events` accepts only certified event types. In this phase that is
`webhook.test` alone: Phase 5 ships the delivery substrate and no
event family (decision D6), and a closed allowlist is what stops a
partner building against an event that would never fire.

`url` must be a public HTTPS target. It is validated here and
**revalidated on every redirect hop** at delivery t

Undelivered events queued for this subscription are deleted with it.
A partner who removed a subscription is not owed its backlog, and
keeping those rows would leave an outbox nothing ever drains.

Scope `webhooks:manage`. D7 class C.

An id from another workspace — and an id that is not well-formed —
answers `resource_not_found`, indistinguishably.

Scope `webhooks:read`. D7 class A.

Every subscription in the caller's workspace, newest first. The
signing secret is **never** in a read: it is returned once at
creation and once at each rotation, and nowhere else — a read that
could return it would make `webhooks:read` a credential grant.

`next_cursor` is always present and always null here: subscriptions
are few enough that this listing is not paginated, and a client's
"loop while next_cursor is not null" must still terminate.

Scope `webhooks:read`. D7 class A.

item.name: Queue a webhook.test event for this subscription

request.description:
Answers **202**, not 200: the event is durably queued, not delivered.
A 200 would claim an outcome the outbox exists precisely because
Postora cannot yet know — the worker delivers on its own cadence and
its own retry ladder.

Refused when the subscription is disabled, or is not subscribed to
`webhook.test`.

Scope `webhooks:manage`. D7 class C — classified by RISK, not
billability: this makes Postora issue an outbound request to a
partner-supplied URL.

Returns the new secret once, and keeps the previous one verifying for
a bounded overlap (`previous_secret_expires_at`, 24 hours) so a
rotation is not an outage while the receiver deploys the new value.

A delivery captures its secret **version** when it is enqueued, so an
event already on the retry ladder is still signed with the secret that
was current when it occurred — its `X-Postora-Event-Id` is immutable,
and one event id arriving under two signatures would be
indistinguishable from a repla

Only the fields present in the body are changed. Setting
`is_active: true` is how an endpoint disabled by an exhausted retry
ladder is brought back: it clears the disabled reason and the failure
count with it.

Scope `webhooks:manage`. D7 class C.

item.name: Get quota and usage for this key

request.description:
The charged total for the presented key and the three buckets that sum
to it — reserved (in-flight), confirmed (provider accepted) and
indeterminate (outcome unknown, never refunded). The period is the
calendar month anchored at `last_reset_at`; `period.end` is the first
instant of the next month in UTC. `meters` is extensible so a second
meter can be added without renaming fields.

Scope `usage:read`. D7 class A.

item.name: List the connected tools this key can reach

request.description:
Every tool resolvable by ANY account bound to this key, de-duplicated
by `tool_id`: a tool shared with two bound accounts is listed once.
Visibility is decided by the same resolver the Postora AI agent uses,
so what is listed here is exactly what `POST /v1/tools/execute` will
accept. Tools marked admin-only in Postora are never listed — a key is
not a person, and cannot be the verified admin those require.

`connection` is present only for tools authenticated through a
connected third-party acco

item.name: Mint a link that connects a third-party account

request.description:
Starts an authorisation flow for one connector type and returns the URL
a human must open to complete it. The connection is created for the
key's own workspace; there is no way to name another one.

`{type}` must be a connector type that authenticates through a
connected third-party account. A native connector type — one configured
with credentials in Postora — and an unknown type both answer
`connector_type_not_connectable` (400).

item.name: Get a workspace in the principal's estate

request.description:
Scope `platform:workspaces.read`. Risk class A. Malformed ids and
workspaces outside the principal's estate answer resource_not_found.
Returns metadata only; bootstrap secrets cannot be retrieved.

item.name: Issue a bound workspace key within the principal's estate

request.description:
Scope `platform:keys.manage`. Risk class C. account_id is required and
must belong to the named workspace. The estate check, account binding,
key creation and audit commit atomically. All platform: scopes, legacy
scopes, unknown scopes and non-string scope entries are invalid_request.
An account or workspace outside the estate answers resource_not_found.
The secret is returned once; this operation does not replay secrets.

item.name: List workspaces in the principal's estate

request.description:
Scope `platform:workspaces.read`. Risk class A. Ownership is by principal,
so rotating the platform credential preserves the estate. Descending
keyset pagination on (created_at, workspace_id); never returns keys.

item.name: Provision a workspace and its bootstrap key

request.description:
Scope `platform:workspaces.manage`. Risk class C. Creates an Auth
service owner, then atomically creates the workspace, Direct QR account
placeholder, bound workspace key and audit row. No plan is assigned;
the new owner's signup quota override or free allowance gates its first account.
The partner attests it collected the supplied Direct QR risk consent;
Postora records this as partner_attestation, not a witnessed acceptance.

The bootstrap secret is returned ONLY on the initial 201; store it s

item.name: Revoke a workspace key within the principal's estate

request.description:
Scope `platform:keys.manage`. Risk class C. Revocation and its audit
row commit atomically. An outside-estate key and an already-revoked
key both answer resource_not_found; repeat revocation is not success.

item.name: Execute one capability of a connected tool

request.description:
Runs one capability of one tool on behalf of one bound account, and
returns what the connector returned.

Authorisation is the same rule the Postora AI agent applies: the tool
must resolve for `social_account_id`, and that account must be bound to
this key. An unbound account, an unknown `tool_id`, a tool that does not
resolve for that account, a malformed id, and a tool whose connection
belongs to another workspace all answer `tool_not_found` (404) — the
same answer, so a caller learns nothing

A disabled feature returns `feature_not_entitled` (403). An id outside
the binding returns `resource_not_found` (404) without an account query.
Missing accounts and accounts from another platform also return 404.

The id is the raw account UUID returned as `account_id` by this
collection, not a Meta phone number id or a prefixed `/v1/accounts` id.
